ROLL CALL: At 6:05 p.m., on Monday, February 8, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met via
video conference, and via teleconference.

COUNCIL PRESENT via video conference: LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER,
PÉREZ
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present physically, via teleconference, and via video conference: City Manager
Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager Tran,
City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Public Works/ Utilities Ray, Director of
Parks and Recreation Macias, Marketing and Communications Specialist Nguyen, Management
Analyst Cuevas, Director of Community Development Castagnola, Fire Chief Phelps, Police
Chief Vu, Director of Human Resources Ko

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Pérez

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-9

The City Clerk reported that she duly gave notice of the regular meeting of the City Council
being held pursuant to the order of the Mayor in accordance with Section 54955 and 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

PÉREZ:  Mayor Pérez requested that Council continue discussion of Item No. 5 and Item
  No. 6 to the next regular City Council meeting. Regarding Item No. 5, Ms. Pérez
  clarified that there was pending litigation against other cities as well as continuing
  discussions within Los Angeles County agencies that may affect Alhambra’s
  ability to enact the ordinance. Regarding Item No. 6, Ms. Pérez clarified that staff
  requested additional time to prepare a report.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ

  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

1.  LEGISLATIVE UPDATE FROM SENATOR SUSAN RUBIO – F2M21-19, F2M20-33

  State Senator Susan Rubio presented to the City Council legislative updates, specifically
  1
2-8-21
   on SB 91 (COVID-19 Relief) and the Eviction Moratorium. The presentation is available
  in the City Clerk’s Office.

  Discussion: Council thanked Senator Rubio for her work and discussed specific items
  from the presentation with her. Councilmember MALONEY discussed the San Gabriel
  Valley Regional Housing Trust and the need for affordable housing in the area.
  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER discussed housing, the 710 Freeway stub,
  education, and COVID-19 testing and vaccination services. Councilmember LEE
  discussed local control over legislation, affordable housing, and the English language
  learner roadmap program. Councilmember MAZA discussed SB91 and SB74. Mayor
  Pérez discussed affordable housing, gentrification, and SB74.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

2.  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 – F2M20-17, R2M21-6

  On June 8, 2020, the City Council adopted the FY 2020-21 Budget, which appropriated
  funds and approved revenue projections for the fiscal year. At the time, Finance Director
  Lieu provided information to the City Council concerning the uncertainties of the full
  impact resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic and uncertainties of revenue and
  expenditure data projections for the last quarter of FY 2019-20 and FY 2020-2021. In
  December 2020, the City Council requested a Mid-Year Budget Review to provide a
  budget update and assessment of the continued impacts of COVID-19 on FY 2020-21.
  Ms. LIEU presented to the City Council an overview of FY 2019-20 actual performance
  and updated budget projections for FY 2020-21. The presentation is available in the City
  Clerk’s office. Staff also requested that the City Council approve a resolution adopting
  Fiscal Year 2020-21 budget adjustments.

  Public Comment received via email on file in the City Clerk’s office: Lewis
  McCammon wrote in support of the Resolution and requested that staff provide
  continued updates.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE and City Attorney MONTES discussed
  developments in the distribution of COVID relief funds with regards to the actions of
  other Los Angeles County agencies. Ms. LEE went on to discuss several line items with
  City Manager BINNQUIST and Ms. LIEU, including General Fund appropriation requests
  from Human Resources and Management Services for contract services and staffing
  services.

  Councilmember MALONEY discussed the overtime pay for Fire Safety employees and
  the later reimbursement from other agencies with Ms. BINNQUIST and Ms. LIEU. He
  went on to the General Fund appropriation request for grant consulting services
  agreement. He reasoned that while the contracted consultant was performing vital work,
  that there was a need for a more full-time position with more direct knowledge of City
  departments and programs. Mr. Maloney proposed using some of the funds to create
  and fund a permanent grant administrator position with City staff who would be able to
  more fully facilitate and oversee the procurement and use of grant funds. Ms.
  BINNQUIST explained the current process in which the responsibility of managing
  grants is handled by each individual department director in addition to their other duties.
  She added that a grant administrator was a typical position for similar sized cities and
  2
2-8-21
   that the position would be very helpful to work with departments and serve as a
  collective hub. Ms. BINNQUIST and City Attorney MONTES discussed the funding of the
  position with Mr. MALONEY as it would relate to the current budget and determined that
  it could be included in the proposed appropriation request of $50,000 for grant consulting
  services for the last three months of the fiscal year. Mr. MALONEY discussed the merits
  of the position and expressed optimism that it would more efficiently acquire and
  administer additional grant funds.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER discussed receiving an update on the costs
  associated with goals on the Strategic Plan with Ms. BINNQUIST. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER supported Mr. Maloney’s suggestion of using funds to create a permanent
  grant administrator on staff and spoke to the benefits of the position. She requested a
  report regarding the grants obtained using the services of CA Consulting from Assistant
  City Manager GARCIA.

  Councilmember MAZA and Ms. LIEU discussed past COVID related reimbursement
  funds and the potential for more from either the Federal government or California State.

  Councilmember LEE referred to Mr. Maloney’s suggestion and expressed that she was
  hesitant to support the expenditure associated with creating a full-time staff position with
  regards to providing salary and benefits. She stressed the need to be financially
  conservative until the end of the consulting grant writer contract. Mr. MALONEY
  addressed Ms. Lee’s concerns and continued to advocate for a permanent staff position
  stating that it would be a long-term cost investment and discussed the need for the
  position.

  Mayor PÉREZ supported the suggestion and discussed the importance of a grant
  administrator based on her personal involvement with non-profits. She stressed the
  importance of the position, the ways it would benefit the City, as well as the budget
  requirements.

  Ms. LEE requested an amendment to Mr. Maloney’s motion to approve the Resolution
  without the inclusion of the grant writing position and to then propose a separate motion
  for that specific position. Mr. MALONEY did not agree to amend his motion and Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER continued to advocate for the position. Ms. LEE stressed that she
  would prefer a staff report to clarify the need to create the position at this time given the
  existing consultant contract and stated that she could consider it in the next fiscal year.
  Mayor PÉREZ called for the vote regarding Mr. Maloney’s motion.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the Mid-Year Budget Review and
  related reports; adopted Resolution No. R2M21-6 entitled: A Resolution of the
  Alhambra City Council adopting Fiscal Year 2020-21 Budget adjustments of the City of
  Alhambra, Golf Course Clubhouse Corporation, Alhambra Capital Improvements
  Corporation, Alhambra Parking Authority, Alhambra Facilities Financing Authority and
  the Alhambra Public Financing Authority; and, directed staff to make appropriate
  revisions to include the retention and recruitment of a full time grant writing staff member
  with the FY20-21 General Fund Appropriations Request from Management Services for
  an increase of $50,000 for Grants consulting services.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ

3.  COUNCIL DIRECTION ON A “COST CONTAINMENT MODE” AND NEW RESERVE
  FUND – F2M20-17, F2M20-7

  City Manager BINNQUIST delivered a staff report. At the December 17, 2020 special
  Council meeting, Vice Mayor Lee requested a discussion on the City entering a “cost
  containment mode” to accumulate unspent funds for the creation of a special
  renter/small business reserve. The City’s current mid-year budget report projects a
  deficit from last fiscal year 2019-2020 and a deficit of the current fiscal year 2020-2021,
  largely due to the pandemic. As such, throughout the pandemic, staff expected
  decreased revenues, and no unnecessary expenditures were undertaken. Should the
  Council wish to direct further spending reductions as part of a “cost containment mode”
  to generate a reserve to assist renters and small businesses, staff would need direction
  on which programs and/or services, if any, should be suspended or eliminated from the
  current budget to provide funding for a new special renter and/or small business reserve
  fund.

  Public Comment received via email on file in the City Clerk’s office: Barbara
  Messina wrote against the suggestion.

  Discussion: Council praised the intent of the proposal as well as the financially
  conservative budget the City has already maintained in response to the pandemic.
  Council also expressed that it may not be necessary at this time for the City to continue
  to cut programs or services given the expected aid which may be available to cities and
  individual citizens through a variety of proposed programs at the federal and state level.
  Councilmember MAZA and Mayor PÉREZ referred to legislation which were discussed
  by Senator Rubio during the presentation in Item No. 1 and by the United States House
  of Representatives and Senate. Council reserved taking action until the outcome of other
  legislation could be known.

  Action Taken:  City Council took no action.

LEE: Councilmember returned to the meeting at 7:49 p.m.

4.  PENSION OBLIGATION BOND/UNFUNDED LIABILITY OVERVIEW – F2M21-26

  At the December 17, 2020 City Council meeting, Councilmember Andrade-Stadler
  requested staff provide an overview of pension obligation bonds. At the same meeting,
  Vice Mayor Lee requested options to reduce the City’s unfunded pension liability.
  Unfunded Accrued Liability (UAL) is the difference between the funds necessary to fund
  retiree benefits, as estimated by an actuary, and then actuarial value of the funds
  already committed to the pension plans to pay those benefits. In other words, how much
  money is needed to pay all retirement benefits already earned by existing and former
  employees if no more money is paid into the system by the City. Director of Finance
  4
2-8-21
   LIEU and Curt di CRISNIS, of Columbia Capital Management presented to the City
  Council a Pension Obligation Bond/Unfunded Liability overview. The presentation is on
  file in the City Clerk’s office.
  Discussion: Council discussed the risks of an Unfunded Pension Liability as it affects
  the City’s standing. Council also discussed the as yet unfunded 115 Trust established by
  the city and supported attempting to contribute to the trust fund rather than investing in
  obligation bonds due to the risks of borrowing from private agencies. Councilmember
  Maloney, Councilmember Lee, and Mayor Pérez supported splitting surplus
  contributions between the Emergency Reserve Fund and the 115 Trust. Ms. LEE
  proposed lowering the Emergency Reserve Fund to below the established 20%
  contribution to enable contributing to the trust fund. Mayor PÉREZ suggested negotiating
  with the City’s various labor groups to see if any were willing to raise the employee
  contribution to PERS.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed this informational report.

5.  PULLED

  COUNCIL DIRECTION ON HERO PAY FOR GROCERY WORKERS – F2M20-33

  At the January 11, 2021 Council meeting, Mayor Pérez requested a discussion about
  Hero Pay for grocery workers. Hero Pay is generally an additional $4 per hour for
  grocery workers due to the greater risk of workplace COVID exposure. Other cities’
  ordinances apply to private and publicly owned grocery stores with over 300 employees
  nationwide and 10 employees locally, and Hero Pay is for a duration of 120 days. The
  County of Los Angeles was considering adoption of such an ordinance until the
  California Grocers Association announced it had filed a federal lawsuit against the City
  of Long Beach arguing the hazard pay is unconstitutional. A hearing on a preliminary
  injunction, which would stop the ordinance from taking effect while the case is pending,
  is set for February 19. In an attempt to avoid a similar legal circumstance, other cities
  are looking to make decisions after the Long Beach hearing. Conversely, some cities
  have moved forward with ordinances, notwithstanding the pending Long Beach lawsuit.
  Staff is seeking Council’s direction as deemed appropriate.

  Action Taken:  No action was taken by Council.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 12)

Council previously voted to continue discussion of Item No. 6 to the next meeting. All other
items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 8, were considered by

6.  PULLED

  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES – SR-710
  MOBILITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT TRAFFIC SIGNAL SYNCHRONIZATION
  PROJECTS – F2M20-67, RFP2M21-5

  The City of Alhambra has identified four major arterials (Valley Boulevard, Garfield
  Avenue, Fremont Avenue and Atlantic Boulevard), that contribute to mobility and
  5
2-8-21
   operational benefits in the SR-710 corridor between I-10 and I-210. The project will
  upgrade the traffic signal system and other components, which will achieve better signal
  synchronization and improve the traffic operations and mobility in the City. Staff is
  seeking to distribute a single Request for Proposals for professional engineering design
  services for the following Traffic Signal Synchronization Projects: Valley Boulevard
  Traffic Signal Synchronization Project – Adaptive Upgrade West City Limit to East City
  Limit; Fremont Avenue Traffic Signal Synchronization Project – Adaptive Upgrade North
  City Limit to Montezuma/I-10 Freeway; Atlantic Boulevard Traffic Signal Synchronization
  Project – Adaptive Upgrade Huntington Drive to I-10 Freeway; and, Garfield Avenue
  Traffic Signal Synchronization Project – Adaptive Upgrade Huntington Drive to I-10
  Freeway.

  Action Taken:  No action was taken by Council.

7.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF ADVANCED METERING INFRASTRUCTURE
  (AMI) WATER METERS – F2M21-6B, C2M21-6, M2M21-15

  The Utilities Department was awarded a WaterSmart and Energy Efficiency Grant
  through the U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Reclamation on September 19,
  2019. The purpose of the grant was to increase the reliability of water supplies and
  improve water management to mitigate impacts caused by drought. In accordance with
  City purchasing and the Grant requirements, a Request for Proposals was issued. After
  a complete evaluation of the proposals, on May 11, 2020, the City Council approved a
  contract by and between the City of Alhambra and Thirkettle Corporation dba Aqua-
  Metric Sales Company for services to provide and install an Advanced Metering
  Infrastructure (AMI) System and purchase of AMI water meters. The AMI system
  significantly has enhanced service by providing improved billing accuracy and more
  efficient customer service. Every year, the Utilities Department is required to purchase
  and install water meters to be placed throughout the City to replace old and
  nonfunctional water meters. Since Aqua-Metric Sales Company was the sole distributor
  of the Sensus Flexnet AMI system and Sensus water meters, the City would need to
  award a contract to Thirkettle Corporation dba Aqua-Metric Sales Company for the
  purchase of AMI water meters. Therefore, staff recommended awarding this contract
  pursuant to AMC 3.36.080(B)2 (sole source).

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra
  and Thirkettle Corporation dba Aqua-Metric Sales Company for the purchase of AMI
  water meters in an amount not to exceed $210,000; and, directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-15)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  6
2-8-21
 8.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF TWO PARATRANSIT PASSENGER BUSES
  FOR ALHAMBRA SENIOR RIDE SERVICES – F2M21-6A, C2M21-7, M2M21-16

  The 2020-2021 fiscal year budget included the replacement of two (2) Alhambra Senior
  Ride Community Paratransit buses. Staff sought approval to enter into a cooperative
  purchase agreement with Creative Bus Sales to finalize the purchase. Cooperative
  purchase was allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080. Staff sought approval
  to piggyback on a cooperative purchase agreement authored by (Cal Act) California
  association for coordinated transportation with (MBTA) Morongo Basin Transit Authority
  and Creative Bus Sales. The purpose of this contract was to provide a variety of transit
  and transportation vehicles including transit buses and mobility vans. Most of the
  vehicles were Federal Transit Administration (FTA) compliant for vehicles purchased
  with FTA grants; Contract # 15-03-CBS.

  Discussion: Mayor PÉREZ, Director of Public Works/Utilities RAY, and discussed the
  City’s goals to move to an electric fleet and the options available for the city via other
  agencies and companies to achieve that goal. Councilmember MAZA, Mr. RAY, and
  Councilmember MALONEY discussed the necessary upgrades to the City’s
  infrastructure to support an electric fleet. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER
  suggested a partnership with another city or the school district to obtain more electric
  vehicles and encouraged working out of a larger regional fleet. Mr. MALONEY
  continued to discuss the need to move away from vehicles reliant on fossil fuels as it
  related to the creation of the City’s Sustainability Plan.

MAZA:  Councilmember Maza disconnected from the meeting at approximately 8:52 p.m.
  and returned shortly thereafter during Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to Creative Bus Sales in an amount not
  to exceed $280,258.52 for the purchase of two (2) Paratransit passenger buses; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-16)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  MAZA

10.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A MODIFICATION TO THE COMPREHENSIVE
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA AND
  THE ALHAMBRA POLICE OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION – F2M21-2, R2M21-4, C87-16C

  The City Council previously adopted the comprehensive MOU with the Alhambra Police
  Officers’ Association (APOA) effective fiscal years 2019 through 2021 at the December
  14, 2020 meeting. Since then, City representatives and APOA members identified a
  need to add language clarifying which APOA members qualified to receive shift
  differential pay and when the benefit pay begins. This amendment was the only mutually
  agreed upon modification to the MOU and all wages, hours and other terms and
  conditions or employment presently in the MOU would remain in full force and effect. A
  resolution approving the modification and memorializing the new language in the revised
  MOU was required.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M21-4 entitled: A
  Resolution of the Alhambra City Council approving a modification to the Comprehensive
  Memorandum of Understanding with the Alhambra Police Officers’ Association,
